8. In June 2014, X travelled to Denver to report on Colorado's then-new recreational cannabis industry. In her hotel room, X purchased a cannabis-infused candy bar from a nearby dispensary. Unaware that edibles typically take an hour or more to produce their effects, and that the bar she had bought was formally labelled as containing multiple separate doses, X consumed the entire bar in a single sitting. She subsequently spent roughly eight hours in what she later described in her column as a 'hallucinatory state', curled up on her hotel-room floor, 'convinced that she had died and that no one had noticed'. The column was published in her newspaper, went viral, and was partly credited with prompting Colorado regulators to introduce mandatory dosing warnings and clearer labelling on cannabis edibles. X has been a columnist at The New York Times since 1995, and won the Pulitzer Prize for Commentary in 1999 for her coverage of the Monica Lewinsky affair. During the 2016 US presidential election cycle, she drew sustained criticism for what many readers considered a false equivalence in her coverage of Hillary Clinton and Donald Trump, having written columns criticizing both candidates in roughly equal measure. ID X.
